senses.gloss:
Ninditāśva (‘possessing contemptible steeds’) is the name of a patron in the Rigveda. The name may suggest connexion with Iran, but such a reference is not at all necessary. Sāyaṇa ingeniously turns the name--probably a nickname-into a compliment by rendering it ‘one who puts to shame the horses of his rivals.’
Foot notes viii. 1, 30.
Hopkins, Journal of the American Oriental Society, 17, 90. Cf. Ludwing, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 159.
Nīnāha, a word occurring once in the Atharvaveda (xix. 57, 4), seems to denote a ‘girdle’ or something similar, as derived from the verb nah, ‘fasten.’
